source_evidence.structural_inspiration: Drill 1: Total distance calculation for a linear velocity model with direction reversal

hints: The particle stops and reverses when $v = 6 - 2t = 0 \implies t = 3\text{ s}$.
Calculate distance on $[0, 3]$: $\frac{1}{2}(3)(6) = 9\text{ m}$, and on $[3, 4]$: $\frac{1}{2}(1)(2) = 1\text{ m}$. Total distance is $9 + 1 = 10\text{ m}$.

walkthrough.text:
Find the instant of rest where the velocity changes sign:
$$v = 6 - 2t = 0 \implies t = 3\text{ s}$$
$$\text{For } 0 \le t \le 3, \quad v \ge 0; \quad \text{for } 3 \le t \le 4, \quad v \le 0$$

Integrate $|v|$ separately over each interval:
$$d_1 = \int_0^3 (6 - 2t)\,\mathrm{d}t = [6t - t^2]_0^3 = 18 - 9 = 9\text{ m}$$
$$d_2 = \left|\int_3^4 (6 - 2t)\,\mathrm{d}t\right| = |[6t - t^2]_3^4| = |(24 - 16) - 9| = |8 - 9| = 1\text{ m}$$
$$\text{Total distance} = d_1 + d_2 = 9 + 1 = 10\text{ m}$$

teacher_walkthrough.text:
Identify turning point:
- Zero velocity timestamp:
$$6 - 2t = 0 \implies t = 3\text{ s}$$

Sum area under velocity graph:
- Forward and return areas:
$$\text{Total distance} = 9 + 1 = 10\text{ m}$$
The particle covers a total distance of $10\text{ m}$.

ai_rubric.observable: Identifies instantaneous rest at $t = 3\text{ s}$ and splits the integration into intervals $[0, 3]$ and $[3, 4]$.
Evaluates forward distance $9\text{ m}$ and reverse distance $1\text{ m}$ to obtain total distance $10\text{ m}$.

source_evidence.structural_inspiration: Drill 2: Distance travelled between two rest instants under negative velocity

hints: Since $v = 3t(t - 4) \le 0$ throughout $[0, 4]$, the distance is the magnitude of the displacement.
Integrate: $\int_0^4 (3t^2 - 12t)\,\mathrm{d}t = [t^3 - 6t^2]_0^4 = 64 - 96 = -32\text{ m}$. Take magnitude: $32\text{ m}$.

walkthrough.text:
Notice that $v = 3t(t - 4) \le 0$ on the interval $[0, 4]$, meaning the particle moves entirely in the negative direction:
$$s(4) - s(0) = \int_0^4 (3t^2 - 12t)\,\mathrm{d}t = [t^3 - 6t^2]_0^4$$

Evaluate the definite integral and take the absolute value for distance:
$$[t^3 - 6t^2]_0^4 = (4)^3 - 6(4)^2 = 64 - 96 = -32\text{ m}$$
$$\text{Distance} = |-32| = 32\text{ m}$$

teacher_walkthrough.text:

- Definite integral:
$$\int_0^4 (3t^2 - 12t)\,\mathrm{d}t = [t^3 - 6t^2]_0^4$$

Compute distance as absolute value:
- Magnitude of displacement:
$$|64 - 96| = 32\text{ m}$$
The distance travelled is $32\text{ m}$.

Evaluate across bounds:

The distance travelled is $56\text{ m}$.

$$d_3 = \left|\int_4^5 (16 - t^2)\,\mathrm{d}t\right| = \left|\left[16t - \frac{t^3}{3}\right]_4^5\right| = \left|\left(80 - \frac{125}{3}\right) - \frac{128}{3}\right| = \left|\frac{115}{3} - \frac{128}{3}\right| = \frac{13}{3}\text{ m}$$

Sum all three segment distances:
$$\text{Total distance} = d_1 + d_2 + d_3 = 12 + \frac{40}{3} + \frac{13}{3} = \frac{36 + 53}{3} = \frac{89}{3}\text{ m} \approx 29.7\text{ m}$$

hints: For $0 \le t \le 2$, velocity is positive. Integrate: $\int_0^2 (12 - 3t^2)\,\mathrm{d}t = [12t - t^3]_0^2 = 24 - 8 = 16\text{ m}$.
For $t > 2$, velocity is negative ($12 - 3t^2 < 0$).
The distance travelled from $t = 2$ to $t = T$ is $-\int_2^T (12 - 3t^2)\,\mathrm{d}t = -[(12T - T^3) - 16] = T^3 - 12T + 16$.
Add the two distances: $16 + (T^3 - 12T + 16) = T^3 - 12T + 32$.

Integrate velocity from $t = 0$ to $t = 2\text{ s}$, where $v \ge 0$:
$$d_1 = \int_0^2 (12 - 3t^2)\,\mathrm{d}t = [12t - t^3]_0^2 = 12(2) - (2)^3 = 24 - 8 = 16\text{ m}$$

Notice that for $t > 2$, $12 - 3t^2 < 0$, so the distance travelled between $t = 2$ and $t = T$ is the negative of the displacement:
$$d_2 = -\int_2^T (12 - 3t^2)\,\mathrm{d}t = -[12t - t^3]_2^T$$
$$d_2 = -[(12T - T^3) - (24 - 8)] = -(12T - T^3 - 16) = T^3 - 12T + 16$$

Add the forward distance $d_1$ and reverse distance $d_2$:
$$\text{Total distance} = d_1 + d_2 = 16 + (T^3 - 12T + 16) = T^3 - 12T + 32$$
